messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan permutation paranoia
parts:
a <- extract(sf, pars="A")
b <- extract(sf, pars="B")
alist <- extract(sf, pars=c("A", "B"))

In all these cases, can I count on the fact that row i for A (whether
buried in the object a or alist) is from the same chain step as row i
for B (in b or alist)?

The documentation guarantees that
a2 <- extract(sf, pars="A)
will return a2 in the same order as a

The R documentation for extract says "For each ï¿½stanfitï¿½ object, the
permutation is fixed (that is, extracing samples a second
time will give the same sequence of iterations as the
previous)."
which suggests that the permutation is property of the stanfit object,
not the individual parameters, and thus the answer to my question is yes.

A related issue is whether the values for A in a will have the same
ordering as the values for A in alist.

Yes seems like the only reasonable answer to my questions; I just wanted
to double-check.

Ross Boylan

P.S. typo for extrac[t]ing in the quoted documentation.
